title: Smithfield Gateway hearings scheduled for October 21 and 28
summary: Smithfield Township scheduled Planning Commission review of the Gateway data-center application for October 21 at 7:00 p.m. and the formal Board of Supervisors conditional-use hearing for October 28 at 6:00 p.m. Both meetings are at J.T. Lambert Intermediate School. Party-status requests will be considered at the October 28 hearing, not the October 21 review.
contextNote: Official township update. Both meetings remain subject to cancellation or postponement. Conditional-use approval would not be construction approval.

title: Lower Towamensing data-center hearing postponed until December
summary: The October 27 Lower Towamensing curative-amendment hearing was postponed at the applicant’s request. Township officials are considering dates during the week of December 14, but no replacement date, time or venue has been confirmed.
contextNote: The December 14, 16 and 17 dates are possibilities, not confirmed hearing dates. Check Lower Towamensing Township before making plans.

title: Residents organize ahead of Lower Towamensing data-center hearing
summary: About 100 people attended an October 1 community meeting ahead of Lower Towamensing Township’s October 27 public hearing on a proposed data-center zoning amendment. The gathering was organized by Save Carbon County and was not an official township hearing. The proposal discussed in current reporting involves the Blue Shamrock Golf Course / DTA Alliance property and a potential large data-center campus.
contextNote: Historical coverage of the October 1 community organizing meeting, which was not the township hearing. The October 27 curative-amendment hearing was subsequently postponed; no December replacement date is confirmed.

title: Project Hazelnut draws new attention over $10,000 household offer
summary: Recent coverage has brought renewed attention to Project Hazelnut, NorthPoint Development’s proposed 15-building data-center campus on roughly 1,300 acres in Hazle Township, Luzerne County. NorthPoint says its $165 million community-benefit package would include $10,000 grants for eligible township households. Hazle Township previously denied the land-development plan, and the developer’s appeal remains in litigation.
contextNote: Wider Northeast Pennsylvania / Pocono foothills reporting. The $10,000 grant is part of a developer commitment tied to the proposed project; it is not an existing public benefit. The township denial remains under appeal and is not final construction approval.

title: Smithfield posts new engineering reviews for Gateway data-center application
summary: Smithfield Township’s Gateway project hub now includes a second township-engineer review and a Monroe County Planning Commission courtesy review. The documents raise unresolved questions involving water capacity, grid reinforcement, acoustical-model compliance, screening, lighting and emergency planning. These are technical review comments, not a decision on the pending conditional-use application, and, at the time, no replacement hearing date had been announced.
contextNote: Official township source. Review comments are not a decision; check the township project hub for hearing notices.

title: Pa. House committee advances bills targeting data-center energy costs
summary: The Pennsylvania House Energy Committee advanced several data-center measures, including proposals addressing when developers must secure electric service, responsibility for grid-related infrastructure costs, and curtailment during power emergencies. HB 2775 would require certain large-load developers to apply for electric service and pay associated fees before seeking zoning approval. HB 2828 addresses infrastructure-cost responsibility and emergency curtailment of data centers.
contextNote: Committee action, not enacted law. The measures advanced from committee and would require additional legislative action before becoming law.

title: Pennsylvania PUC moves to keep data centers subject to grid-emergency curtailment
summary: The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission issued a tentative order seeking comment on proposed changes intended to prevent large data centers from being automatically treated as protected critical load during electricity emergencies. The PUC is also planning a November 17 technical conference on cost allocation for large electric loads.
contextNote: Official regulatory proceeding and tentative order, not a final regulation or an order requiring every data center to shut down during an emergency.

title: U.S. House advances data-center grid-cost protections
summary: The U.S. House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act 417–3. The bill would require state utility commissions to consider standards intended to make data centers larger than 100 MW cover the incremental electricity-generation and transmission costs needed to serve them.
contextNote: Update — Sept. 30: The Senate voted 57–43 to advance the House-passed measure, short of the 60 votes required. The bill therefore failed to advance in the Senate. The proposal would have required consideration of a federal standard rather than automatically setting electricity rates.

title: Data center proposed in Lower Towamensing Township
summary: Property owners filed a curative amendment seeking to allow a data center at the Blue Shamrock Golf Course / DTA Alliance property in Lower Towamensing Township, Carbon County. This wider-Poconos proposal is outside the core Pike and Monroe project tracker.
contextNote: Wider Poconos reporting. The filing is evidence of a proposed land-use change, not a confirmed project approval or a core tracker entry.

title: Smithfield Gateway conditional-use hearing postponed
summary: Smithfield Township postponed the previously advertised September 9 conditional-use hearing for the Gateway data center. A replacement date will be separately advertised; September 23 is a regular Board meeting, not a continuation hearing.
contextNote: Historical public notice documenting the September postponement. Smithfield Township subsequently scheduled Planning Commission review for October 21 and the conditional-use hearing for October 28.

title: Pennsylvania Farm Bureau calls for pause on data-center development
summary: Pennsylvania Farm Bureau released a policy paper arguing for a pause on data-center development to give policymakers and communities time to study the impacts of data centers and their supporting infrastructure, including farmland loss, resources for rural municipalities, and an equitable share of benefits for local communities and ratepayers. This is an advocacy organization’s policy position, not enacted state policy.
contextNote: Advocacy position, not law. The Farm Bureau board voted in July to support a statewide moratorium; the September policy paper explains its reasoning.

title: Salem Planning Commission again recommends 4,000-acre data-center overlay expansion
summary: Salem Township’s Planning Commission again recommended expanding its Special Data Center Overlay District by more than 4,000 acres for the proposed 4-3 Glenbrook Group project. The matter now moves to the township Board of Supervisors, expected to consider it in October. The Planning Commission recommendation is not final construction approval.
contextNote: Northeast PA reporting outside the Pike and Monroe project tracker. A planning-commission recommendation is advisory; the Board of Supervisors decides.

title: Coming to some of Pennsylvania’s most picturesque places: data centers
summary: Reporting from the Tobyhanna area explores how proposed data centers could affect forests, waterways and the Poconos’ rural character.

title: Pike County, PA DEP inviting comments on substation transmission line project
summary: DEP’s stormwater-permit review covers the Bushkill Falls–Birchwood Lakes transmission segment through Lehman and Delaware townships, with stream, wetland and land-disturbance concerns.

title: What we know about Smithfield Gateway data center proposal
summary: An early look at the Smithfield Gateway data center proposal, including how data-center development became part of the long-planned commercial site and what the initial concept looked like when it reached local review.
contextNote: Plans have changed since this article was published. Its earlier two-building concept was superseded by the August 2026 revision: one two-story building, approximately 500,000 sq. ft. total, a 250,000 sq. ft. footprint and proposed 250 MW load. See the current project record below.

title: What Shapiro’s new data center order does — and doesn’t — force developers to do
summary: An explainer of Pennsylvania’s new data-center executive order: what it requires of developers, where discretion remains, and what is still unresolved.

title: DATA CENTERS: Residents fear negative impacts on water resources as data centers are proposed across Northeast Pa.
summary: WVIA examines private wells, groundwater and cooling demand. Water use depends on the cooling system and site design; facilities do not all have the same needs.

title: DATA CENTERS: Industry’s power consumption worries NEPA residents concerned about property values, electric rates
summary: Who pays for new power demand? WVIA explores residents’ concerns, utility perspectives and the uncertainty around rates and grid upgrades.

title: DATA CENTERS: Local governments, residents at odds with NEPA projects despite promises of economic growth
summary: Jobs and tax revenue meet local concerns in the final installment of WVIA’s series on Northeast Pennsylvania’s data-center debate.

title: FirstEnergy’s Shawnee-Walker 69kV transmission-line project
summary: Pike County residents gathered in Delaware Township to organize opposition to FirstEnergy’s Shawnee–Walker transmission project, circulate petitions, and raise concerns about property impacts, land clearing, eminent domain, and the project’s necessity.
contextNote: This is reporting on community opposition. Claims by organizers are attributed to them, not independently verified here.

title: Pike County Commissioners address proposed 69kV transmission line
summary: Pike County commissioners weighed the need for electrical reliability and future economic development against resident concerns about property impacts, routing, and eminent domain associated with the Shawnee–Walker transmission project.

title: Board of Supervisors discusses proposed FirstEnergy transmission line project
summary: Dingman Township supervisors heard resident concerns about the Shawnee–Walker project, including possible effects on private property, environmental resources, electricity rates, and questions from residents about whether future industrial or data-center development could benefit from the added capacity.
contextNote: Residents’ speculation about future warehouses or AI facilities is not evidence that Shawnee–Walker was designed specifically for data centers.

title: Possible Data Center in Pike?
summary: A community post raised questions about whether a large DEPG-owned property near Route 739 in Dingman Township could someday be repurposed for data-center development, particularly as new electrical infrastructure is considered nearby.
contextNote: Community report · Unverified. This post republishes Facebook speculation. No public application, announced operator or confirmed data-center plan was identified in the sources reviewed for this property.

title: Majority of Monroe County municipalities have data center ordinances
summary: A countywide look at municipalities adopting or considering data-center ordinances as development proposals move through local planning.

title: Pennsylvania governor signs order imposing new rules to set up AI data centers in state
summary: Reuters reports on Gov. Shapiro’s executive order and its intended environmental, community-participation and energy-accountability measures.

title: Data centers are ‘redefining’ midterm races across Pennsylvania
summary: Data-center development has rapidly become a major Pennsylvania political issue, with candidates across competitive races taking positions on electricity costs, local authority, environmental protections, and the pace of new development.

title: Committee votes on Sen. Brown’s statewide data center moratorium amendment
summary: State Sen. Rosemary Brown proposed a three-year statewide moratorium on hyperscale data-center development, arguing that Pennsylvania needs time to address unresolved questions involving energy demand, water use, infrastructure, environmental impacts, and community planning.
contextNote: The proposed three-year moratorium amendment failed 2–9 in committee, according to this report. It did not become a statewide moratorium.

title: Bresnahan’s proposed legislation aims to keep control local over data center development decisions
summary: U.S. Rep. Rob Bresnahan introduced legislation aimed at protecting municipalities that reject data-center proposals from costly federal litigation while also encouraging local workforce commitments when projects are approved.
contextNote: Proposed federal legislation; this is not a statement that these protections are already law.

title: Is this the future of America?
summary: Loudoun County’s data-center growth brought major tax benefits—and debate over noise, power lines and development pressure. A look at the tradeoffs after years of expansion.
contextNote: Outside case study: Loudoun County, Virginia. This is context for the Poconos, not a local project report.
